messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Team project: Goal is at least 3,500 m. With 4 m/s wind it still has to land inside 2,000 m of the pad. We want dual deploy on this one. Thanks.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Apogee at least 3,500 m. Wind is 4 m/s and the rocket has to land inside 2,000 m of the pad, so drift is capped. Dual deploy: drogue at apogee, main at a lower altitude. Rail, angle and site are not stated, so 1.5 m vertical rail and sea level. Landing speed is not stated, so the 6 m/s gate applies.

2. Feasibility: A single chute from 3,500 m at 6 m/s takes 3,500 / 6 = 580 s. At 4 m/s of wind that descent walks past a 2,000 m pad limit, which is why the team asked for dual deploy. Drag-free speed at 3,500 m is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 3,500) = 262 m/s, and a real rocket with a recovery bay will need an L-class motor rather than a small K. Looking up a 54 mm L.

2. Feasibility: HP-L1000W is an AeroTech L, 2702 N*s, 991 N average, burn 2.72 s, diameter 0.054 m, length 0.635 m, mass 2.19 kg. The only delay is 18 s, which is one ejection, not dual deploy. The motor flies plugged. An altimeter opens the drogue at apogee and the main at 250 m. The motor fits a 58 mm tube: mount OD 0.055 m leaves an inside diameter of 0.054 m for the motor, and the tube ID at 0.058 m with a 0.001 m wall is 0.056 m, so the mount fits.

3. Size: Liftoff guess 3.4 kg with the motor, a 1.20 m tube and two chutes. Thrust-to-weight is 991 / (3.4 * 9.81) = 29.7. Weight is 3.4 * 9.81 = 33.4 N, rail acceleration (991 - 33.4) / 3.4 = 282 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 282 * 1.5) = 29.1 m/s. Drogue for about 2 kg at 18 m/s: area 2 * 2 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 324) = 0.124 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.124 / pi) = 0.40 m. I will fly 0.50 m. Main for about 2 kg at 5 m/s: area 2 * 2 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 25) = 1.60 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 1.60 / pi) = 1.43 m. I will fly 1.7 m so the landing stays under 6 m/s. The fast drogue is what keeps the drift inside 2,000 m at 4 m/s.

4. Draft: 58 mm fiberglass, tube 1.20 m, ogive nose, four fiberglass fins, AeroTech HP-L1000W plugged, 0.04 kg altimeter, 0.50 m drogue at apogee, 1.7 m main at 250 m. Wind 4 m/s, 1.5 m rail.

4. Check: The simulator gives 3886.3 m, above the 3,500 m floor. Drift is 895 m, inside 2,000 m. Landing is 3.9 m/s, under 6 m/s, so the main is the canopy at touchdown. Margin is 2.53 cal at rail exit and through the burn. Rail exit is 35.2 m/s, thrust-to-weight 30.5. The drogue opened at 21.2 s, at apogee, at 5.5 m/s. Wind is 4 m/s. The section reached the ground in 320 s. Peak Mach is 2.07, with the supersonic body-calc warning.

5. Fix: nothing left that fails.

6. Uncertainty: Liftoff mass is 3.32 kg, close to the 3.4 kg guess. The output shows one deploy time, the apogee drogue, and not a separate main-opening time. The landing speed is what tells me the main opened. Chute Cd is 0.8 on both. The motor's 18 s delay was not used.
